questions.q: What is a Wildly Important Goal?
a: The one goal with the biggest impact
A goal that is easy to reach early
A long list of related objectives
A target chosen by the whole team
questions.why: Lesson 1 says you must prioritise a single goal that makes the most difference.

questions.q: What does the peach tree example illustrate about goals?
a: Focusing on a few gives better results than spreading thin
Good goals take several seasons to bear fruit
Competition improves the quality of your work
Pruning is a useful metaphor for cutting costs
questions.why: Lesson 1 explains that thinning the tree lets a few peaches grow far better than many mediocre ones.

A result you can only check at the end
A number showing last month’s output
A target handed down from above
questions.why: Lesson 2 defines lead measures as the actions, such as exercise, that produce the lag measure.

questions.q: Why does the summary compare a scoreboard to children playing soccer?
a: Keeping score motivates people to work harder
Children need clear rules to learn teamwork
Games teach players to accept defeat gracefully
Coaches should track every player’s mistakes
questions.why: Lesson 2 notes that without a score, kids have little reason to push for goals.

questions.q: What should a weekly WIG meeting cover?
a: Last week’s commitments, the scoreboard and the plan ahead
Budget figures, staff reviews and new hires
Team grievances, salaries and promotions
Long-term strategy, markets and competitors
questions.why: Lesson 3 lists those three steps as the way to stay accountable and keep progress steady.
